mediation_note: The legacy streaming channel table had no usable regulation row, while the extension now shows a directly observable licensing-transparency wedge between the domestic public tariff benchmark and YouTube Music. This does not identify a royalty-rate gap, but it does fill the previously unobserved regulation channel with a measurable comparability object.

The bundle-side undercut is about 2.51 times the mechanical gross-sales benchmark for Melon regular under the public 10.5 percent branch. This means regulation-side pass-through may matter, but it is too small on its own to explain the same-country bundle pressure now visible in the extension.

The legacy risk channel did not indicate Korean disadvantage in the mixed composite, but the extension isolates a strong same-service matched FY2025 tax-burden gap. This is a within-channel subcomponent that the old composite appears to have diluted rather than a contradiction of the whole risk story.

The broad service-cost share gap is very small in the matched pair, so the extension keeps the risk channel from being overread as uniformly large across all cost components. This is a tempering row inside the same risk channel.

The extension adds a domestic governance and verification-cost subchannel that was not explicit in the legacy cost/risk composite. This row is one-sided and bounded, but it helps explain why foreign-platform disputes can be harder to verify cleanly even when price competition is observed elsewhere.

The legacy market-transfer channel was small in the mixed firm composite, but the extension shows a materially larger same-country bundle undercut when the product comparison is done inside Korea at the consumer-plan level. This is a scope-driven reframe rather than a replacement of the legacy market row.

The extension supplements the market-transfer channel with a pre-remedy demand-lead proxy: within the common May 2025 tracked-app set, YouTube Music's usage-share proxy exceeds Melon's by 13.4813 percentage points. This does not estimate realized diversion, but it adds a plausible demand-side mediation path.

The extension adds a future bargaining and lock-in layer to the market-transfer channel: the full YouTube bundle is KRW 5590 cheaper than separate purchase of Lite plus Music Premium inside the same provider family. This is a dynamic concentration proxy rather than a contemporaneous welfare estimate.

The extension explicitly keeps the actual foreign-versus-domestic licensing-rate gap unestimated. This row is included so the newly activated regulation channel cannot be overstated as proof of a known preferential foreign contract rate.

The extension also keeps the Korea-facing foreign-product tax-incidence gap unestimated. This prevents the stronger matched annual tax-burden row from being misread as a point estimate of Korean service-level tax underpayment.
